藏品名称_EN: Tiger eating sheep bronze ornamental plaque
描述_EN: Bronze Plaque with Tiger Eating Sheep，the Han dynasty (206 BC-220 AD)，elder9.2centimetre，surname Kuan4.9centimetre。　　Bronze Plaque with Tiger Eating Sheep塑造的是一只刚刚捕获到猎物的猛虎口衔羊颈的状态，Lifelike reproduction of a tiger in the steppe moments after it has caught its prey.，vivid and evocative。Bronze plaques are carved on one side，Showing a tiger biting the neck of a goat，A vivid scene of the weak and the strong，It symbolizes the wearer's courage in riding on the grassland.。　　The ornamental plaque is the most reflective of the cultural and artistic characteristics of the early pastoral peoples of northern China among the Ordos bronzes。Most of the motifs are carved in relief、translucent carving and other techniques，Decorated with realistic or abstracted animal motifs。Most of the tattoos on the plaques show animals fighting to the death.、The content of the weak and the strong，To show the spirit of courage。
描述_ZN: Tiger skin three color skewed bowl, Kangxi, Qing Dynasty, 5.4 cm high, 12.5 cm in diameter, 5.8 cm in foot diameter.　　Bowl skewed mouth, curved belly, ring foot. Yellow, green, purple and white glaze spots inside and outside. White glaze inside the footrim. The outer bottom signed in blue and white regular script "Kangxi year of the Qing dynasty" six double-line peripheral blue and white double circle paragraph.　　Tiger skin three color porcelain for the Kangxi plain three color porcelain in a novel variety. Ware table with yellow, green, purple, white and other color glaze dyed into the patchy, like a tiger skin pattern, so commonly known as "tiger skin glaze" or "tiger skin three color", the heirloom products are mostly seen in bowls, plates and other types of ware.
